newsitem.title: SWEDEN: EU must create jobs for EMU to work - UK's Blair.
newsitem.headline: EU must create jobs for EMU to work - UK's Blair.

text.p: A European Union single currency, whether weak or strong, risks coming under great strain unless EU member states reform their economies to tackle unemployment, British Prime Minister Tony Blair said on Friday.
He warned fellow centre-left leaders that neither the single European market nor the single currency could ever work unless governments showed their citizens that Europe's agenda was their agenda.
The way to do that, Blair said, was to restructure Europe's economies to make job creation an attainable objective.

"EMU cannot work if it is set up on the basis of a fudge. Whether it looks like a weak currency or a strong one, if it masks unreformed economies, strains in the system risk being too great," Blair told European socialists at their annual congress in the Swedish city of Malmo.
"There is no comfort in size alone. A united, unreformed European economy will be no better than a disparate, unreformed European economy," Blair added.
Blair said the institutions of Europe were as out of touch, out of date and unresponsive to the needs of people as the Conservative Party became in Britain.
Blair's Labour Party heavily defeated the Conservatives in elections on May 1.
British people were not alone in feeling that Brussels was not in tune with their priorities, he said.

"That sense of alienation from the European ideal is consistent throughout much of Europe. We will only remove it by showing that Europe's agenda is their agenda. That comes back to jobs," Blair said.

He urged his counterparts to follow his lead in putting flexible labour markets and skills at the top of their economic agenda and warned them that their voters would not be patient or forgiving if they failed to rise to the challenge.
Blair's government has enjoyed an unprecedented honeymoon in its first five weeks but Blair said honeymoons did not last for ever.
"What matters is that the public remember what we said we would do, and we do it... I am determined that my government will not be a 100-day wonder, but a force for change which endures," he said.
